label: Second-personal competence includes capacity for self-accountability
definition: The capacity to recognize addressed moral demands and the standing of an accountable community, and to regard oneself as answerable through self-directed reactive attitudes such as guilt. Merely calculating another person's interests or complying for instrumental reasons does not automatically instantiate this capacity.
note: Darwall, p. 8. The separate substantive step from this competence to equal authority to hold fellow agents responsible is not true by definition.
